description: Validated reusable production lessons only. Do not store unverified assumptions as lessons.

lessons.problem: Characters animated with static kit poses (40/64 acts), planner 2-frame walks and glides: mechanical, rigid, sliding.
lessons.root_cause: acts authored with blocking poses (stand, knock, hold_up...) and walk=True; film.json had no tween, so poses snapped; motion polish (breath/blink) only runs on library moves
lessons.fix: every act is a registered m:<id> library move; position changes use m:walk/run/bike with linear travel at real speeds; tween {ones:true, face_frames:0, move_blend:6}; new moves are registered in templates/motion_styles/library.mjs; gate D runs tools/anim_audit.py

tools/tests/test_production_intelligence.py :: PI-001 anim_audit PASSes the current film
verification.regression_check: anim_audit on the v1 film.json (git c3937a0) reports STATIC 37 -> FAIL; current film PASS

lessons.problem: Effects silently disappeared (shell bursts, river moonlight, a fade) although node --check passed and the film rendered.
lessons.root_cause: an inline // note written after code on a long one-line statement swallowed the rest of the line
lessons.fix: inline notes use /* */; tools/lint_set_modules.py flags a // that follows code and is followed by code; gate E runs it on every episode set module

tests: tools/tests/test_production_intelligence.py :: PI-002 lint catches swallowed code (fixture)
tools/tests/test_production_intelligence.py :: PI-002 Ghost Army set module is clean
verification.regression_check: the lint flags the bug in git history (commits 63d3a57, 6759b96) and 3/3 fixture lines, 0 false positives on the 2 clean fixture lines and on the current set

lessons.problem: A character entering a new place slid for 0.5 s from its old coordinates after the cut, and the place switched one frame before the position (a 1-frame pop).
lessons.root_cause: film_plan baked a place-entering act as a normal move (default move_s 0.5) keyed one frame after the body/place key
lessons.fix: film_plan.py: an act that enters another place lands on the same frame as the place switch (_land), no move

tests: tools/tests/test_production_intelligence.py :: PI-003 entering a place never slides
verification.regression_check: the test strips every move_s from place-entering acts and bakes: before the fix 4.52 m one-frame pop (lou f319) and 0.5 s slides; after 0.00 m

lessons.problem: Framing gates (head cut, figure size) measured figures that are not in the shot's place.
lessons.root_cause: the plan checker's framing loop ignored st.place while the renderer hides off-place figures
lessons.fix: film_plan.py framing loop skips a figure whose place differs from the camera's place

tests: tools/film_plan.py check episodes/ghost-army/film.json

lessons.problem: A wide white haze over the night river.
lessons.root_cause: the moon key light glinted on the reflective water toward the camera and the bloom spread it (found by zeroing light groups one by one)
lessons.fix: night key light placed on the camera side; water specularIntensity lowered; reflection kept through the env map
lessons.notes: scene-specific; promote only when seen in a second film

lessons.problem: Characters placed inside a hero object's footprint (lifters inside the hull) and the object floating above their hands.
lessons.root_cause: positions chosen by eye in plan space without the object's measured footprint and contact height
lessons.fix: compute the object's footprint in plan space (rotation included) and stage contacts on its sides; check with tools/frame_checks/check.mjs body_in_mesh

tests: node tools/frame_checks/check.mjs episodes/ghost-army/film.json (0 body_in_mesh FAIL in the hook)
verification.regression_check: frame checks report the old staging as body_in_mesh FAIL (tank_track) and the new one clean

lessons.problem: The finish level of a film was judged by eye; the Ghost Army v1 preview was far below the user's fortress reference (detail 0.047 vs 0.095, saturation 0.72 vs 0.40, 5.3 % still frames, 9 hard cuts vs 0) without any check saying so.
lessons.root_cause: no measured standard: the look bible was provisional and no tool compared a preview with the reference
lessons.fix: official fortress standard (references/REFERENCE_LOOK_BIBLE.md v2.0, production/config/reference_standard.json); tools/reference_compare.py measures the reference and every film with the same code; production_controller.py compare-reference writes production/REFERENCE_COMPARE.md and gate F reads it (WARN preview, FAIL final)

tests: tools/tests/test_production_intelligence.py: reference standard: fortress PASS, v1 preview FAIL
verification.regression_check: the fortress passes all 10 thresholds; the v1 preview fails 9 of them

lessons.notes: Image statistics do not judge modelling quality: the bible's minimum-standards table and a reviewer with images remain required.

lessons.problem: A pod was deleted before its results were downloaded: the 92-minute stage-8 lock was lost.
lessons.root_cause: pod.py delete terminated the pod with no check of what it held; results lived only on the container disk; the watchdog also removed pods.
lessons.fix: pod.py: manifest.json (path, size, sha256) published by every pod stage, fetch with sha256 check and FETCH_RECEIPT, delete refused unless every listed file is present locally with the same sha256; explicit logged overrides only; watchdogs STOP pods (volume kept).

tests: tools/tests/test_pod_guard.py: 13/13 PASS (fake pod over local HTTP)
verification.regression_check: not yet run on a real RunPod pod

lessons.problem: The three.js -> glTF lock flattens every surface to one colour: painted textures, vertex colours and instance colours are lost before Blender.
lessons.root_cause: GLTFExporter writes the material base colour; canvas maps, vertex colour and InstancedMesh instanceColor are not carried by the lock materials.
lessons.fix: Do not build a film's look on a lossy export: worlds are built natively in Blender (Mission 0 architecture).

lessons.problem: A LookDev that replaces the approved palette with photographic PBR colours fails (Ghost Army prototype: wrong colours everywhere).
lessons.root_cause: Poly Haven textures were used with their own albedo; display transform AgX not calibrated against the approved frames; generic HDRI light.
lessons.fix: LookDev is palette-first: place palette is data, PBR maps give relief/roughness/wear and are tinted to the palette, every place is calibrated against the reference with numbers before CB sees it.

lessons.problem: Blender's glTF importer turns each GPU instance into its own object (field: 50,656 objects for 202 meshes).
lessons.root_cause: EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing is expanded on import.
lessons.fix: Repeated things are instanced inside Blender (geometry nodes / collection instances); a QA gate counts objects vs instances.

tests: blender 5.2.2 import probe of out/lock/sets/field.glb: 50656 objects, 202 meshes

lessons.problem: An effect that reads state kept from the previous render makes a frame depend on frame order (sound rings: 4.5 % of pixels differ between a slice and a single still).
lessons.root_cause: scene.onBeforeRender stored the camera, the next update used it.
lessons.fix: Every animated value is a function of the frame number only (baked keys in Blender); a determinism test renders frames alone and in sequence and requires identical pixels.

verification.regression_check: reproducibility test interrupted, NOT RUN

lessons.problem: Poly Haven's API answers 403 to the default Python User-Agent.
lessons.root_cause: the API filters generic clients
lessons.fix: Send a client User-Agent (RicksClips-LookDev/1.0).

tests: LookDev job 005 downloaded assets after the fix

lessons.problem: Blender RenderSettings.resolution_percentage is an int: a float (37.5) raises TypeError and the job still exits 0.
lessons.root_cause: bpy property type; the job runner only read the exit code
lessons.fix: Use int percentages or set resolution_x/y; job runners must scan logs for Traceback/TypeError, not only rc.

tests: LookDev job 003 ran after the fix

lessons.problem: Two renders of the same Blender frame gave different sha256 although the pictures were the same; with the denoiser on, a frame rendered after another differed by 1/255 on 0.7 % of pixels.
lessons.root_cause: Cycles writes its timings (total_time, render_time) as PNG text chunks; the OIDN denoiser keeps state between renders of one process.
lessons.fix: rc.render strips PNG text chunks after each write and turns stamps off; determinism is tested without denoise (bit-identical) and the denoise tolerance is 1/255.

tests: tools/tests/test_rc.py: determinism frame alone == frame after frame 0 (sha256 equal)
verification.regression_check: 3 repeated pairs bit-identical on a fresh scene (2026-11-18)

lessons.problem: Characters and props appeared, disappeared, teleported or shrank in view: the hero 'appears suddenly' out of the car (shot 1); in shot 2 a young-driver card was swapped for the hero at frame 158, teleported from the cockpit to the track at 143, and the 3D helmet popped in. CB reported the same kind of error twice.
lessons.root_cause: Each case was fixed locally without a rule or a check, so the next shot repeated it; a change of state was built as a visibility/location switch instead of an animated action; and the 2D move-to-move blend silently does nothing when the two moves are drawn in different views (puppets.mjs moveOf), so arms snapped between moves.
lessons.fix: CB_RULES 11h: everything happens through an action, the camera never stops, real surfaces and shadows. demos/crashed_car/shots/continuity.py runs on every built shot BEFORE any render (render_layers.sh refuses to render on FAIL): POP, TELEPORT, SHRINK/GROW, POSE_POP, HOLD; BREAK (a whole replaced by its own pieces) and FX are reported as allowed. tools/card_anchors.py measures head, feet, hands and pose pops on every drawing (card_service runs it automatically) so 3D props follow the drawn head/hands. Shot analyses get a mandatory section 'Entrées / sorties / changements d'état'.

tests: continuity.py on the old s02_pit build: 7 POP, 2 TELEPORT, 1 HOLD (FAIL, the reported errors)
continuity.py on the new s02_pit and s02_corner: PASS 0/0/0
continuity.py caught a new helmet side-swap at 223 in s02_corner; fixed, PASS
verification.regression_check: render_layers.sh refuses to render a part whose continuity report is not ok

lessons.problem: A fresh session (handoff) could not pass tools/tests/test_rc.py: 2 FAIL (library: vintage_bicycle glb missing; cards: episodes/ghost-army/out/plan/camera_baked.json missing) although the code was right. Blender itself was missing (download.blender.org not in the environment's allowed hosts).
lessons.root_cause: Files outside git were produced once by hand: a throw-away bike2glb.py (gltf -> 1k glb) never committed, and a film_plan bake the test silently assumed. The handoff listed what to re-download but not how to rebuild derived files.
lessons.fix: tools/gltf_to_glb.py (re-packs the scaled textures: the glTF importer packs images, so scaling alone exported the original 2048 px bytes, 34.5 MB instead of 3.7 MB); test_rc bakes the plan itself when out/ is missing; scripts/restore_untracked.sh restores every untracked input idempotently (Sketchfab models, glb conversions, baked plan); asset.json fetch_note gives the exact rebuild command.

restore_untracked.sh rebuilds a deleted glb, second run converts nothing

lessons.problem: Chosen by name, two library moves did not act what the plan said: lift/B raises the arms above the head (hands at 1.38 m) instead of bending to the ground, and sit/A (front) stays standing for ~0.9 s before it sits, then sits on an invisible seat (feet 0.14 m off the ground).
lessons.root_cause: Moves were picked from their id/feeling labels without measuring what the drawing does over time; there is no front-view 'sit on the ground' move.
lessons.fix: Measure every chosen move on the drawings (card_anchors.py head_top / feet / hands per frame) before building; start a move at the right moment with the pose offset syntax 'm:<id>@<seconds>' (puppets.mjs); preview candidate moves side by side with templates/motion_styles/render.mjs --still. Shot 1 uses inspect/B (squat, hands low) and m:sit/A@0.7 (the plop lands on the word), the hidden seat sunk 0.30 m into a tall grass tuft.

anchors after: squat 1.65 m at 12-18, plop 30-36, seated from 48; 0 pose pops
verification.regression_check: card_service prints anchors; read head_top/feet per act before building

applies_to: every move chosen from the motion library

lessons.problem: Falling leaves teleported (70 TELEPORT) and an acorn cap popped: a random delay was drawn INSIDE the per-frame loop, and a child object was not hidden with its parent.
lessons.root_cause: Randomness must be drawn once per object, never per frame; a visibility switch on a parent does not carry to children.
lessons.fix: Random values drawn once per object before the frame loop; no visibility switch for a thing that goes into a hole: it sinks under the surface that covers it. continuity.py caught both before any render (the check works as the permanent guard).

tests: continuity before: POP 1, TELEPORT 70 (FAIL)
continuity after: PASS 0 everywhere
verification.regression_check: render_layers.sh refuses to render on a continuity FAIL

lessons.problem: A 'hard cut' at frame 96 written in the analysis did not exist: shots 1 and 2 are ONE continuous take (the camera swoops down at 102-120). Building them as two cut shots would have broken the continuity of the set, the car and the character.
lessons.root_cause: An improvised per-frame difference detector with a fixed threshold (14) took a 14.1 motion peak for a cut, while the repository tool (tools/analyze_reference.py, shots.json) correctly found no cut before 22.9 s.
lessons.fix: Shot boundaries come from tools/analyze_reference.py shots.json; every boundary is checked at 30 fps around it before a shot is planned (a cut is a one-frame spike, a camera move is a ramp over several frames). A shot that continues the previous take is built ON TOP of the previous shot's script (s02_crash imports s01_plant.build_take), so set, car, card and camera are the same objects.

tests: per-frame difference 88-176: no one-frame spike; ramps at 101-121 and 150-176
continuity.py on s02_crash (frames 96-176): PASS 0 everywhere
verification.regression_check: shots/sNN.md must cite shots.json and the 30 fps check of each boundary

lessons.problem: A wheel detached from the Sketchfab car rolled around the wrong point and never tipped over flat.
lessons.root_cause: glTF parts keep their origin at the model origin (the car centre), not at the part's centre; the tip-over was applied about the axle instead of about the rolling direction.
lessons.fix: Before animating a part on its own: move its mesh origin to its bounding-box centre (mesh.transform(-c), world matrix @ T(c)); spin about the axle, tip about the path direction (s02_crash.wheel_off).

tests: key frames 126-149: wheel rolls, wobbles, lies flat from 134; continuity PASS
verification.regression_check: look at the part on 3 key frames after detaching it

applies_to: every part detached from an imported model

lessons.problem: CB: no cinematic light. No sun rays, the trunk dark in full daylight, a flat painted sky, grass too tall, too dense and the wrong green, a grade unlike the reference, and a glittery car paint.
lessons.root_cause: The look was judged by eye on our own frames, never MEASURED against the reference. The sun was front-lit (the reference is backlit). No fill light under the big crown. The sky was a gradient with mesh clouds. The Sketchfab paint kept its metallic/roughness texture and normal map.
lessons.fix: Cinematic kit in sets/roadside.py: visible HDRI sky (Poly Haven, rotated so its sun matches the sun lamp), backlit sun, bounce_fill area light (camera-side, invisible), thin haze volume + light_shafts attached to the tree, shorter and half-dense grass recoloured to measured values. Grade = Standard + Medium Contrast, exposure -0.35, saturation 1.05, chosen by measuring 5 transforms. tools/grade_match.py compares key frames with the reference (luma, saturation, contrast) and must PASS before a preview. Car paint: the asset's texture, metallic, roughness and normal links removed (they made it sparkle), then a SMOOTH METALLIC white (metallic .55, roughness .28, coat .6) as CB asked; untinted glass. Grass: CB found it too dark and dull -> ramp #4e8a2e..#a4d866 (hue 90 vs reference 87-96, lightness .34-.39 vs .29-.38), exposure -0.5.

tests: grade_match before: frame 126 luma 0.65 vs 0.49, frame 46 saturation 0.12 vs 0.35 (FAIL)
grade_match after: frames 0, 46, 126, 149 PASS
verification.regression_check: tools/grade_match.py on the key frames of every shot

lessons.problem: CB's corrections kept repeating the same family: flat road without wear or tyre marks, flat untextured farmland behind the fence, a fence without realism or shadow, grass on one side of the road only, a sky or sun that did not match the reference. Each was fixed in one shot, then found again in the next.
lessons.root_cause: Corrections were applied to the shot, not to the method: the first version of a new set started from flat or default values, and nothing in plan_check or the helpers refused it.
lessons.fix: All corrections are now DEFAULTS: blender/rc/look.py (visible HDRI sky rotated to the sun, hard sun, bounce fill, sun shafts, light haze, scanned PBR with relief, road wear: wheel paths + tar snakes), roadside.py (furrowed fields, real fence with varied posts, sagging wires and shadows, same green verge on both sides, LOD grass), plan_check LOOK + vehicle checks (a plan without look is REFUSED: test_plan_check), docs/CORRECTIONS_CB_FR.md (every correction -> rule -> where it is enforced), continuity.py CLIP (camera far clip cuts the set).

plans s01-s03 and the example: PLAN PASS with look blocks
continuity PASS with CLIP 0; set moved to rc.look: frame 262 identical (0.00/255)
verification.regression_check: python3 tools/tests/test_plan_check.py

lessons.problem: The camera far clip (Blender default 100 m, then 1000 m) cut the set: the fields stopped and the sky showed where the farmland goes on to the horizon (aerial view).
lessons.root_cause: No check compared the camera's clip_end with how far the set reaches.
lessons.fix: continuity.py CLIP: fails when a big flat set piece reaches farther than clip_end and prints the fix (cam.data.clip_end = N). Default clip_end 4000 m in the shot camera.

tests: continuity before the fix: CLIP 1 (set reaches 2588 m, clip 1000 m)
after: CLIP 0

applies_to: every shot with a far horizon

lessons.problem: Aerial view: the oak's shadow was a small soft blob toward the camera instead of the long hard shadow of the reference; no fence shadows; measured contrast 0.14 against 0.21.
lessons.root_cause: The visible HDRI sky also LIT the scene at full strength: its own photographed sun (48 deg high) cast a second short shadow and its fill washed out the shadow of the sun lamp. The sun lamp was not the dominant light.
lessons.fix: rc.look.sky_hdri: for every ray but the camera's the sky is capped (no hot sun) and dimmed (light=.5): the lamp is the only sun. Sun height and direction MEASURED on the reference shadow (length / object height, direction on the ground): crash_instinct -48 deg, 15 deg. A sun-only debug render (world strength 0) shows what the lamp really does.

tests: frame 180 before: contrast 0.14, shadow 1 crown long; after: contrast 0.20 (ref 0.21), shadow crosses the road and the far verge; grade_match PASS on 180 and 262
verification.regression_check: grade_match.py on the key frames of every shot

lessons.applies_to: every daylight exterior with a visible HDRI sky

lessons.problem: From the air the grounds were flat colours with visible repeating squares: one green, brown fields instead of golden rows, a light grey road.
lessons.root_cause: A scanned texture tiled every 2-4 m averages to ONE colour from 15 m up; a multiply tint over a dark scan cannot reach a light target colour; a grazing/high camera needs its own measured values.
lessons.fix: rc.look.tex: recolor (the scan keeps its detail, takes the measured colour), untile (second bigger turned copy mixed by noise), macro (3-25 m patches lighter/darker), stripes (regular rows readable from the air). Target colours are sampled on the reference frame, not guessed.

tests: frame 180: fields #86735a -> gold/ochre/straw rows; road near #6c6c68 -> dark blue-grey; saturation 0.29 (ref 0.30)
verification.regression_check: key frame from the highest camera of the film, side by side with the reference

lessons.applies_to: every ground seen from a high or far camera

lessons.problem: Backlit grass tufts were either dark (sun only) or flat neon green (sky fill): the tree's shadow did not show on the grass.
lessons.root_cause: Blades were opaque: with the sun behind, the camera only sees their shadow side.
lessons.fix: Grass and leaves let light through (Translucent mixed at .45 into the blade material): they glow in backlight and the shadows of big objects read on them.

tests: frame 180: the oak shadow is readable on the right verge
verification.regression_check: key frame with the sun behind the subject

lessons.problem: A fresh session on another account lost 40 minutes on the environment: Blender 4.0 installed instead of 5.2.2, textures and models blocked, Sketchfab token refused, the SUV model missing.
lessons.root_cause: The cloud environment (allowed hosts, network secrets) is an account setting, not in git; the Sketchfab secret was saved as Bearer while an API token needs the prefix Token; restore_untracked.sh did not list the SUV.
lessons.fix: restore_untracked.sh downloads the SUV too and says which prefix the secret needs; HANDOFF 0 lists the environment check first (get the environment, hosts of CLOUD_NETWORK_DOMAINS.txt, secret with prefix Token, verify with /v3/me = 200).

tests: api.sketchfab.com/v3/me: 401 with Bearer, 200 with Token; test_rc 27/27 after restore
verification.regression_check: first step of every new session

lessons.problem: The second imported car came out white instead of blue: the paint was applied to the first car's material.
lessons.root_cause: bpy.data.materials.get('body') returns the FIRST material of that name; the second import's material is 'body.001'.
lessons.fix: Materials of an imported model are collected from the imported objects' own slots (dict by base name), never looked up by bare name.

tests: key frame 324 before: white car; after: blue #2f74d8, clear glass
verification.regression_check: key frame of every imported vehicle

lessons.applies_to: every scene with two imported models

lessons.problem: Shot 4 was lit with the aerial view's backlight: the tree, the sign and the posts were dark, the sky white; CB: 'the scene is too dark, give me exactly the reference's lighting'.
lessons.root_cause: The light was copied from the previous view instead of being read on the reference for THIS view; the reference re-lights each view (shadow of the sign falls behind it: sun on the camera's side).
lessons.fix: Each shot analysis has a table 'clue on the reference -> light' (shadow direction and length, lit faces, sky, glow, fill). rc.look.relight() changes sun, sky rotation, glow and fill together on one frame, off-frame inside a whip.

tests: frame 309: luma 0.52 -> 0.42 (ref 0.45), saturation 0.27 -> 0.36 (ref 0.40); sky blue; sign and posts lit
verification.regression_check: grade_match on the key frames of every view
